bibliography: Four distinct studies, each listed with its duplicate records. (A) vSTMD: Mingshuo Xu, Hao Luan, Zhou Daniel Hao, Jigen Peng, Shigang Yue. 'vSTMD: Visual Motion Detection for Extremely Tiny Target at Various Velocities'. arXiv 2501.13054 (cs.CV), v1 22 Jan 2025, v2 18 Jan 2026; no journal reference; the v2 text says it 'has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication' and the README says 'under review'. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13054 ; HTML v2 https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13054v2 . Code: https://github.com/MingshuoXu/vSTMD (Python + MATLAB + notebooks; folders demo/, comparison_models/, experience_in_RIST/, experience_in_XS-VID/, maritime/ (SeaDronesSee demo), timecost_analysis/; 31 commits, 9 stars, no license shown; README says only a subset of code and data is released, full implementation after publication). What changed between v1 and v2 was not checked [uncertain]. (B) Feedback STMD: Hongxin Wang, Huatian Wang, Jiannan Zhao, Cheng Hu, Jigen Peng, Shigang Yue. 'A Time-Delay Feedback Neural Network for Discriminating Small, Fast-Moving Targets in Complex Dynamic Environments'. IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems 34(1):316-330, 2023 (online 2021), DOI 10.1109/TNNLS.2021.3094205 (bibliographic data from OpenAlex). Preprint duplicate of the same study: arXiv 2001.05846, title 'Time-Delay Feedback Neural Network for Fast-Moving Small Target Discrimination Against Complex Dynamic Environments', v1 29 Dec 2019 to v5 28 Jun 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.05846 . Follow-up (not examined in full): 'Mathematical study of neural feedback roles in small target motion detection', Frontiers in Neurorobotics 16:984430, 2022, DOI 10.3389/fnbot.2022.984430; and 'Spatio-Temporal Feedback Control of Small Target Motion Detection Visual System', arXiv 2211.10128. No code repository found for (B) [uncertain]. (C) Attention-and-prediction-guided STMD (apg-STMD / ApgSTMD): Hongxin Wang, Jiannan Zhao, Huatian Wang, Cheng Hu, Jigen Peng, Shigang Yue. 'Attention and Prediction-Guided Motion Detection for Low-Contrast Small Moving Targets'. IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics 53(10):6340-6352, 2023, DOI 10.1109/TCYB.2022.3170699 (from dblp / Lincoln blog). Preprint duplicate: arXiv 2104.13018, v1 27 Apr 2021 to v7 23 Apr 2022 (13 pages, 21 figures; an intermediate version v3 was titled 'Attention-Prediction Guided Motion Detection for Low-Contrast Small Targets' with different author order), https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13018 . Also in University of Leicester repository (figshare 24796710). No public code found [uncertain]. (D) Fu and Yue: Qinbing Fu, Shigang Yue. 'Modelling Drosophila Motion Vision Pathways for Decoding the Direction of Translating Objects Against Cluttered Moving Backgrounds'. Biological Cybernetics 2020, DOI 10.1007/s00422-020-00841-x ; preprint duplicate arXiv 2007.00886 (q-bio.NC), single version 2 Jul 2020, 27 pages, 13 figures. IMPORTANT correction to the task description: arXiv 2007.00886 is NOT a review of insect motion detectors for robots; it is an original hand-designed model of Drosophila ON/OFF motion pathways with HS/VS wide-field read-out (it only contains a literature-review section). The actual review by the same authors is probably Fu, Wang, Hu, Yue, 'Towards computational models and applications of insect visual systems for motion perception: a review', Artificial Life 25(3), 2019 [uncertain: not opened in this check].
full_text_checked: (A) vSTMD: arXiv abstract page and HTML v2 full text up to ~100k of 139k characters (method, datasets, Tables I-III, ablation, runtime, future work); final ~39k characters (likely appendix/references) not read; GitHub README and file tree read, code not executed. (B) Feedback STMD: arXiv abstract page and ar5iv HTML full text (method Eq. 8-11, Table I-III, Figs 8-16, limitations); IEEE version not accessed. (C) apg-STMD: arXiv PDF (latest version) full text extracted and read for attention module (Eq. 3), prediction module (Eq. 19-23), memorizer, facilitation experiments (Figs 14-21) and conclusion; the quantitative ROC comparison against DSTMD, ESTMD, STMD Plus is only in the supplementary material, which was NOT accessed; IEEE version not accessed. (D) Fu and Yue: arXiv abstract page and ar5iv HTML full text (stimuli, Figs 5-13, Table 2, limitations); Biological Cybernetics version not accessed. The Fu-Wang-Hu-Yue 2019 review was not opened.
task_and_output: (A) vSTMD / vSTMD-F: detection (localization) of extremely tiny moving targets plus estimation of their motion orientation; output is a per-pixel STMD response map, thresholded and passed through non-maximum suppression to give target positions, with an orientation estimate per detection from the Collaborative Directional Gradient Calculation. No bounding box size, no identity, no tracking. (B) Feedback STMD: per-pixel, per-direction small-target response map; detections are pixels above a threshold; the point of the paper is to shift velocity preference towards fast targets and suppress slow background false positives. No identity or tracking. (C) apg-STMD: per-pixel directional STMD output E(x,y,t,theta), a facilitated output Q, and a prediction map M(x,y,t) for the next frame; detections are thresholded positions with direction; the prediction map gates where the attention module enhances contrast in the next frame. It is detection with recurrent spatial priming, not identity-preserving tracking. (D) Fu and Yue: global direction of a translating object, read out as the signed membrane potentials of horizontal (HS) and vertical (VS) wide-field systems; no localization, no detection map.
data_and_independent_videos: (A) RIST real-world dataset: 19 videos, 29,900 frames total, natural scenes (sky, buildings, trees, grass, shrubs; sunny and cloudy); synthetic Vision Egg videos with panoramic backgrounds (number of sequences not stated); XS-VID used for a cross-task comparison (sequence count not stated); maritime SeaDronesSee demo in the repository only. Since the model is learning-free there is no train/test split; parameters are fixed (Table I) and, per the lineage, tuned by hand, so evaluation on RIST is not a held-out test of tuned parameters in the ML sense [uncertain whether any parameter was tuned on RIST]. (B) Vision Egg synthetic: six groups of videos varying target size, luminance, target velocity, background velocity and background direction, 1000 frames each; three synthetic multi-target videos; RIST real: the paper describes 16 videos (GoPro Hero 6, 240 fps), and only 6 were used for ROC evaluation (Fig. 16). No training, no split. (C) Vision Egg synthetic dataset plus RIST (the paper states 19 videos, GoPro Hero 6); hand-tuned parameters (Table I), no train/test split; number of videos used in the ROC comparison is not stated in the main text (supplementary not accessed). (D) Synthetic Vision Egg stimuli (clean and cluttered, two natural backgrounds) and a few real camera recordings (pedestrians, a vehicle, grouped pedestrians, windblown vegetation); number of real recordings not stated; no training, no split.
target_size_and_input_resolution: (A) Input 480x270 px (RIST) and 470x310 px (synthetic), one pixel per 'ommatidium'; targets defined as 1 to 8^2 pixels (extremely tiny); synthetic targets 5x5 px; the paper notes orientation is unreliable for large targets. (B) Input 500x250 px (synthetic), 480x270 px (RIST); RIST targets 3x3 to 15x15 px; default synthetic target 5x5 px; Feedback STMD width preference below 20 px peaking at 10 px, height optimum 5 px (Fig. 12b-c). (C) Input 500x250 px (synthetic), 480x270 px (RIST); RIST targets 3x3 to 15x15 px; default synthetic target 5x5 px; model responds to widths below ~18 px and heights below ~13 px, peaking at 5x5 px (Fig. 10c-d). (D) Input 320x180 px (clean) and 700x180 px (cluttered); target bar 25x120 px; size sweep 10x10 to 100x100 px (Fig. 12) with larger targets giving stronger responses; authors note ~126,000 pixels versus ~8,400 ommatidia in a fly. For comparison: our eye has 721 hexals and the median target box is ~9.37 x 12.06 lattice steps, i.e. the target covers a large fraction of the eye, unlike STMD targets that cover a few pixels of a 130k-pixel image.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: (A) RIST at 240 Hz; synthetic velocities 0.1-10 px/frame; dynamic backgrounds influenced by ego-motion in both datasets. (B) Synthetic sampling 1000 Hz; RIST 240 fps; background motion simulated (e.g. 150 px/s); camera handheld/moving in RIST. Performance drops when background is faster than the target (Sec. IV-E). (C) Synthetic 1000 Hz, RIST 240 fps; moving backgrounds (e.g. 250 px/s in Fig. 11). (D) 30 fps synthetic, background moving -5 to -200 deg/s; fails to suppress background at -200 deg/s (Fig. 13); authors note 30 Hz versus ~250 Hz in flies. Only (D) operates at our 30 Hz, and it has no localization; all STMD localization results are at 240-1000 Hz.
detector_and_exemplar: None of the four uses an external object detector or an exemplar/template of the target. (A)-(C) detect any small moving target bottom-up; in (C) the only 'memory' is the prediction map from previous detections, which primes locations, not appearance. (D) has no target specification at all; it reports global direction.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: None in all four: all are hand-designed, learning-free models with fixed parameters. (A) vSTMD parameters in Table I (e.g. sigma1=1, alpha=0.25, A=1, B=3); the authors list a hybrid learnable medulla-like module as future work. (B) Table I: retina sigma1=1; LMC Gamma kernels n1=4, tau1=8, n2=16, tau2=32; Tm1 n3=9, tau3=45; feedback alpha=1, n4=10, tau4=25, eta=1.5; lateral inhibition A=1, B=3, sigma2=1.5, sigma3=3. (C) Table I: attention kernel scales {2.0,2.5,3.0,3.5}, orientations {0, pi/4, pi/2, 3pi/4}; LMC n1=2, tau1=3, n2=6, tau2=9; prediction kernel zeta=2, eta=2.5; facilitation decay kappa=0.02; beta and mu constants (values of beta, mu not found in Table I [uncertain]). (D) parameters 'decided empirically' (Table 2), feed-forward, no training.
controls_seeds_splits: No seeds (deterministic models) and no data splits in any of the four. Controls are ablations and matched hand-designed baselines: (A) ablation vSTMD vs vSTMD-F (feedback adds ~25% localization, ~40% lower orientation error); baselines ESTMD, DSTMD, Frac-STMD, STMD+, ApgSTMD, FeedbackSTMD, F-STMD, LC11/LC18 models, and optical-flow networks RAFT, SEA-RAFT, StreamFlow, MemFlow, FlowDiffuser, DPFlow (orientation only); no learned small-object detector on RIST was found in Table III [uncertain]. (B) Feedback STMD vs the same network without feedback, plus ESTMD and DSTMD 'tuned to match the same velocity and size ranges'; parameter sweeps of alpha, n4, tau4 (Fig. 13). (C) facilitated vs unfacilitated output (Figs 14-21), with vs without attention module (Figs 12-13); ROC vs DSTMD, ESTMD, STMD Plus only in supplementary. (D) ablation removing vDoG and FDSR pre-filters (Fig. 11), 4 vs 8 correlators (Fig. 10). No shuffled or random-network controls anywhere; no confidence intervals.
metrics_and_numbers: (A) vSTMD, RIST, Table III (means over videos): vSTMD mAUC 47.35, mAR 38.64, mAP 28.06, mF1 32.44, AAE 0.71 rad, 608 FPS GPU; vSTMD-F mAUC 59.38, mAR 46.18, mAP 34.46, mF1 39.33, AAE 0.50 rad, 567 FPS GPU; best natural baseline Frac-STMD mAUC 45.65, mAR 31.43, mAP 20.66, mF1 24.88. Relative mF1 gains: ~30% (vSTMD) and ~58% (vSTMD-F) over Frac-STMD (abstract). AAE of vSTMD-F 32.4% below DPFlow (0.74 rad) and 39% below ApgSTMD (0.82 rad). CPU: 168 FPS (vSTMD), 161 FPS (vSTMD-F) on i5-12500; GPU RTX 3050 Laptop. Table II (synthetic AAE by velocity): vSTMD-F best average rank, strongest at 0.6-3 px/frame, minimum AAE 0.21 rad. Note an internal inconsistency: Sec. V-C1 calls the vSTMD gain over Frac-STMD 'marginal, ~7%', which conflicts with Table III. Detection threshold and distance tolerance for true positives not stated in the read part [uncertain]. Absolute performance is low: mF1 39.33 means most tiny targets are still missed or confused at 240 Hz. (B) Feedback STMD: metrics detection rate DR = TP / number of targets and false alarm FA = false positives / number of images (Eq. 17-18), TP within a distance threshold (stated as 5 px [uncertain]); ROC curves Fig. 14a, 15a-c, 16a-f. At fixed FA = 10 (Fig. 14b-f): DR stays above 0.9 for targets 6x6 to 15x15 px while baselines drop to 0; above ~150 px/s baselines fall to 0 while Feedback STMD stays high beyond 400 px/s; worse than baselines when the background is faster than the target. Velocity optimum shifts from 150 px/s (no feedback) to 350 px/s (feedback), preferred range 150-800 px/s (Fig. 12a). Runtime 0.084 s/frame vs 0.064 (ESTMD), 0.116 (DSTMD) (Table III, MATLAB, i7 2.2 GHz). Outperforms ESTMD and DSTMD on all six RIST videos (Fig. 16) - read from ROC plots, no table. (C) apg-STMD main text has qualitative/curve evidence only: unfacilitated response peaks within 7-8 ms, facilitated response builds higher (Fig. 14); facilitation increases contrast sensitivity and direction selectivity (Figs 16-18); occlusion on a circular path (R = 50 px, occlusion angle 30 deg): facilitated output keeps spreading forward during occlusion while unfacilitated output is near zero, and the output reaching the occlusion end point decreases as occlusion angle and radius grow (Figs 20-21). ROC comparison vs DSTMD, ESTMD, STMD Plus is only in the supplementary material (not accessed); the authors state 'greatly improved detection performance' for extremely low-contrast targets and failure for targets with no contrast. vSTMD's Table III gives ApgSTMD AAE 0.82 rad on RIST (an independent re-measurement by the same group). (D) Fu and Yue: no accuracy metrics; only HS/VS output traces and their median/mean/variance (Fig. 9); qualitative claims: correct direction for rightward targets over cluttered backgrounds, failure at -200 deg/s background (Fig. 13), pre-filter ablation breaks decoding (Fig. 11).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: not applicable in the ML sense for all four (no training); (A) evaluates on RIST and XS-VID with fixed parameters - yes as 'not fitted', but parameters may have been hand-tuned on the same lineage of data [uncertain]. Target absence (refusal): no in all four; no metric for frames without a target, though FA per image in (B) penalizes background false positives. Similar distractors: (B) yes partially - multi-target synthetic videos (Fig. 15) and slow small-target-like background features; (C) yes partially - two small targets in one scene (Fig. 11); neither tests choosing one particular target among similar ones; (A) not reported; (D) distractors only as windblown vegetation. Occlusion: (C) yes, only a synthetic circular-path transient occlusion (Figs 19-21); (A), (B), (D) no. Night or low light: no in all four; (C) addresses low contrast (Weber contrast sweep) in daylight images, RIST includes cloudy scenes only. Sequential operation on own predictions: (C) yes - the prediction map is computed recursively from the model's own detections and fed back each frame; (A)-F and (B) feed back the model's own output (temporally delayed in B, instantaneous t-dt in A); none evaluates drift or error accumulation of this loop over long sequences. Moving camera: (A), (B), (C) yes (RIST handheld, synthetic moving backgrounds); (D) moving background only. 30 Hz: only (D); all STMD localization tests at 240-1000 Hz.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanisms: (1) Time-delay output feedback (B): the STMD output at a pixel and a Gaussian-weighted sum of its neighbours are delayed by a Gamma kernel (n=10, tau=25 at 1000 Hz, i.e. ~25 ms) and subtracted from both medulla channels (Tm3, Tm1) before their multiplication; this suppresses slow responses and shifts velocity tuning upward; it is suppression, not re-finding. (2) vSTMD-F (A): an instantaneous feedback pathway from t-dt into the cross-inhibition dynamic potential and correlation stage (Eq. 8-9), plus cIDP to widen velocity tuning; it improves localization ~25% and orientation ~40% over vSTMD on RIST. (3) Prediction-guided facilitation (C): from each detection's position and direction, a ring-shaped, direction-biased prediction kernel centred at distance v_opt*dt ahead (Eq. 20) spreads activity forward; the predictive gain is a leaky recursion F_t = kernel * (mu*E_t + (1-mu)*F_{t-dt}) (Eq. 21); its integral over directions is the prediction map M that (i) selects image regions where an attention kernel (orientation-minimum Laplacian-of-Gaussian-like speckle detector) enhances contrast in the next frame and (ii) is added to the STMD output with exponential decay (Eq. 23, kappa=0.02) - 'facilitation'. During occlusion the facilitated trace propagates forward and fades with occlusion duration. This is modelled on dragonfly CSTMD1 predictive facilitation (Wiederman/O'Carroll lineage, ref [24] in the paper). (4) Fu and Yue (D): ON/OFF pre-filtering (vDoG, FDSR) plus ensembles of local correlators feeding HS/VS wide-field cells; direction read from global HS/VS signs; no prediction or memory. Proposed modification (ours, not published): transplant only the idea of (3) - a leaky, motion-extrapolated, direction-biased spatial prior over the eye, computed from the fly's own previous read-out of the lost target, that multiplicatively or additively gates FlyVis input contrast or the read-out map during loss. This is our proposal; no source tested it with large targets or at 30 Hz.
transfer_limits: 1) Frame rate: all STMD localization evidence is at 240 Hz (RIST) or 1000 Hz (synthetic); the Gamma-kernel delays and the 7-8 ms facilitation build-up are tuned for 1-4 ms steps. At 30 Hz (33 ms step) one frame already exceeds the feedback delay of (B), and motion between frames for our targets is a sizeable fraction of the crop; the correlator-based STMD stage itself would alias. Only Fu and Yue run at 30 Hz, and they report no localization metric. 2) Target size: STMDs are tuned to 1-15 px targets (peaks 5x5, rejection above ~18-20 px), i.e. lateral inhibition deliberately suppresses large objects; our targets are ~9x12 lattice steps on a 721-hexal eye, i.e. they fill a large part of the field. The STMD core (lateral inhibition, small-target selectivity) is therefore the wrong filter for us; only the prediction/facilitation wrapper is size-agnostic, and even its kernel (ring at v_opt*dt, zeta=2 px) must be rescaled to box size. 3) Moving and rescaling crop: our eye recentres and rescales around the track prediction every frame, so 'image coordinates' of the prior must be transformed between frames (state transfer under crop change); the STMD papers assume a fixed camera image. Ego-motion in RIST is moderate; (B) itself fails when the background is faster than the target. 4) Identity: none of these models keeps target identity or an exemplar; facilitation primes any target that appears in the predicted ring, so a similar neighbour crossing the ring would be facilitated as well - exactly our failure mode (find the previous target among similar neighbours or refuse). 5) Refusal: no source evaluates target absence; facilitation actually biases toward false positives in the predicted region during occlusion, which is the opposite of a reliable refusal. 6) Environment: YOLO/ByteTrack/MASA already provide a Kalman-type motion prior (ByteTrack predicts box position); a leaky extrapolated prior duplicates the Kalman prediction, so any gain must be shown beyond the tracker's own motion model (variant B without FlyVis). 7) Grey 721-hexal input: compatible in principle (STMDs also use grey luminance), but the attention kernel scales (2-3.5 px) are tied to pixel-sized speckles. 8) Metrics: F1/AUC/DR-FA on per-frame detections, not HOTA or identity metrics; absolute vSTMD-F mF1 of 39.33 shows tiny-target detection remains weak even at 240 Hz.
research_questions_addressed: Q1 (recognize a specific target among similar ones and refuse): caution - none of the four provides an exemplar-based selection or refusal; apg-STMD's prediction-guided facilitation is a spatial-prior mechanism (where to look), not an identity mechanism (which one); it primes any target in the predicted region. The relevant insect mechanism for selecting one of two targets (CSTMD1 selective attention, Lancer et al. 2019) is outside this lineage and was not checked here. Q2 (representation vs readout): no direct evidence - all models are hand-designed with no learned readout or probes. Q3 (conditions under which mechanisms work): direct evidence and strongest contribution - STMD localization is shown only at 240-1000 Hz, targets 1-15 px (peak ~5 px), images ~480x270 px, with moving backgrounds slower than the target; Fu and Yue at 30 Hz report no localization metric and fail at fast background motion; so the outline's condition 'tested on moving camera at 25-30 Hz with targets > 5 facets' is NOT met by any source in this lineage. Q4 (joint position and refusal): no evidence. Q5 (one testable mechanism): design analogy - the only cheap, size-agnostic piece is the leaky motion-extrapolated prior with gated input contrast (apg-STMD Eq. 19-23), which can be implemented with no extra trainable parameters and checked within a 12 GB budget; but its benefit must be separated from the tracker's own motion prediction.
candidate_node_change: Node: state transfer / input gating of FlyVis during target loss ('prediction-gated eye'). Change: keep a leaky prior map P over the hexal lattice, P_t = warp_crop(P_{t-1}) * decay + kernel(direction, speed) applied to the fly's last confident target read-out (adapted from apg-STMD Eq. 21-23, kernel width scaled to the box size ~9x12 steps, decay chosen per 33 ms frame), and use it either (i) to gate input contrast to FlyVis photoreceptors inside the predicted region (attention-module analogue) or (ii) to bias the existing spatial read-out map (facilitation analogue). The warp between frames must account for crop recentring and rescaling. This is a node of the fly path (input preparation / state), consistent with the project boundary, but it has no learnable novelty in the fly core and largely duplicates a Kalman prior. Controls: (1) stand without change; (2) the same prior applied directly to the readout of variant B (network without FlyVis, ~9602 params) or simply as a Gaussian prior around the ByteTrack prediction - this isolates the prior's own value; (3) prior + stock frozen FlyVis (variant C) and + trained FlyVis (D). FlyVis result only if (3) beats (2). Minimal check (cheap, on cached data, no new training): on the existing loss episodes of Z13, measure the share of useful centre corrections and false re-finds on similar neighbours with and without the prior, for C and B, paired by episode; then, only if positive, one HOTA run with MASA and paired bootstrap by video. Stop condition (write before the run): stop if the prior does not raise useful corrections by more than the gain of the same prior on B, or if it raises false re-finds on similar neighbours (the expected failure mode, since facilitation is identity-blind), or if paired HOTA CI includes zero after one full run. Expected outcome given the literature: likely a gain attributable to the prior itself, not to FlyVis; this candidate is therefore low priority unless combined with an identity mechanism.
strongest_objection: The lineage solves a different problem: bottom-up detection of pixel-sized targets at 240-1000 Hz with hand-tuned temporal kernels, without identity, exemplar, refusal, or tracking metrics. Its only re-finding mechanism (prediction-guided facilitation in apg-STMD) is shown only on one synthetic circular-path occlusion and is identity-blind, so in our setting (similar neighbours, 30 Hz, large targets, moving and rescaling crop) it would most likely facilitate the wrong neighbour, and whatever it adds is essentially a leaky Kalman-style spatial prior that ByteTrack already provides and that works equally without FlyVis. Quantitative evidence for the prediction module is in an unaccessed supplementary, and the strongest numbers (vSTMD-F) are from an unreviewed preprint with an internal text-table inconsistency.
evidence_strength: (A) vSTMD: preprint (arXiv v2, under IEEE review), code repository verified to exist but partial and unlicensed, not executed; no independent replication; weak-moderate for tiny-target detection, weak for our decision. (B) Feedback STMD: peer-reviewed (IEEE TNNLS 34(1), 2023), no code found, synthetic plus six real videos read off ROC curves, follow-up by the same group only; moderate for its own claim, weak for our decision. (C) apg-STMD: peer-reviewed (IEEE TCYB 53(10), 2023), no code found, quantitative comparison only in supplementary (not checked), occlusion evidence synthetic and qualitative; weak for our decision. (D) Fu and Yue: peer-reviewed (Biological Cybernetics 2020), not a review, no metrics; weak and largely irrelevant to localization. All four come from one research group (Yue, Peng, Lincoln/Guangzhou), with no independent replications found [uncertain]. Overall: weak.
